# @aliziodev/singapay

> Unofficial TypeScript SDK for the SingaPay payment gateway (Indonesia).
> Framework-agnostic, server-only, zero runtime dependencies. Node 20+, Bun,
> Deno, edge runtimes — all cryptography via Web Crypto.

This file is a dense brief for AI agents writing integration code. It exists
because several things below are **not guessable** and fail silently if got
wrong. Full prose: [README.md](README.md). Working on the repo itself:
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## Minimal use

```ts
import { SingaPay } from '@aliziodev/singapay';

const singapay = new SingaPay({
  environment: 'sandbox',                    // defaults to sandbox, never production
  clientId: process.env.SINGAPAY_CLIENT_ID!,
  clientSecret: process.env.SINGAPAY_CLIENT_SECRET!,
  apiKey: process.env.SINGAPAY_API_KEY!,     // dashboard calls this the API Key
  accountId: process.env.SINGAPAY_ACCOUNT_ID!,
});

const link = await singapay.paymentLinks.create({
  reff_no: 'INV-1001',
  payment_link_type: 'total',
  total_amount: 150_000,
});

link.data.payment_url;
```

Endpoint groups: `paymentLinks` `paymentLinkHistories` `virtualAccounts`
`vaTransactions` `qris` `ewallet` `card` `subscriptions` `directDebit`
`disbursement` `ewalletMoneyOut` `qrisMoneyOut` `accountTransfer`
`cardlessWithdrawal` `accounts` `balance` `statements`.

## Things you will get wrong

**`apiKey`, not `partnerId`.** The dashboard labels it *API Key*; the gateway
receives it as the `X-PARTNER-ID` header. Swapping it with `clientSecret` is
the most common setup mistake and fails as an unexplained auth error.

**Lists are in `items`, not `data`.** `data` is always an object; every
`list()`-style endpoint puts its rows in `items` (`null` for single records,
`[]` for a genuinely empty list). Reading `data` on a listing returns `{}`.

**Server-only, and enforced.** Every request is signed with the client secret.
The package throws on import in a browser. Send only public artefacts to the
client: `payment_url`, `qr_string`, `virtual_account_no`, `checkout_url`.

**Money-out is off by default.** Every fund-moving call throws
`MoneyOutDisabledError` until `moneyOut: { enabled: true }`.

**Never retry money-out.** `SP001`/`SP005` arrive as
`IndeterminateOutcomeError` and mean the outcome is *unknown*, not failed. Call
`inquireStatus()` with the same reference number. A blind retry duplicates a
real transfer.

**On the card product, `SP001` is overloaded** — it also means malformed
`card_expiry` and daily-quota-exceeded, both definite refusals. Read the
message before treating it as ambiguous.

**Transfer and its pre-flight checks use different field names:**

| Call | Bank field | Account field |
|---|---|---|
| `disbursement.transfer()` | `bank_code` (3 digits or SWIFT) | `bank_account_number` |
| `checkFee()` `checkBeneficiary()` | `bank_swift_code` (SWIFT only) | `bank_account_number` |

**Amounts come back inconsistently typed** across events — `"125000.00"` from a
VA, `55000` from an e-wallet. Always funnel through `Amount.from()`. Outbound
amounts must be integers; floats are refused before signing.

**`card_expiry` is YYMM**, not MMYY. December 2030 is `3012`.

**The gateway silently drops unknown fields.** A misspelled key is not an
error — the call succeeds and the field is simply absent from the result.
Assert what you sent came back, not merely that the call succeeded.

## Webhooks

```ts
import { readWebhookBody } from '@aliziodev/singapay';

const verified = await singapay.verifyWebhook(
  await readWebhookBody(request),   // web Request, Node req, or an h3 event
  request.headers,
  '/api/webhooks/singapay',         // exactly as registered, query string included
);
```

**Verification tries every configured connection's secret.** One callback URL
receives deliveries signed by *different* credentials — money-out and the
expiry sweep come from the merchant Default credential even when a Specific one
made the call. Declare the other credentials under `connections` or those
deliveries 401 silently.

**A permission refusal has two shapes** and only one carries a code:
`403 SP403 "This account requires its own credential…"` and
`403 (no code) "Access denied to this account."` Branch on
`error.status === 403`, not on the code.

**Payload shapes differ per event.** `transaction-expiration` is a *batch* of
three arrays, not one transaction, and never sweeps e-wallet.
`payment_method_additional` is a JSON **string** on `payment-link-inquiry` but
`payment.additional_info` is an **object** on `ewallet-native-transaction`.

**A paid payment link never says how it was paid** — `data.payment.method` is
always the literal `payment_link`. The real channel is in the earlier
`payment-link-inquiry` delivery; join on `reff_no`.

## Deployment

SingaPay rejects unregistered IPs with `SP017`. **Vercel, Netlify and
Cloudflare Workers use dynamic egress IPs and cannot be whitelisted.** Call
from a static-IP host, or route through a static-IP proxy that forwards path,
headers and body **byte for byte** — a re-serialized body breaks the signature.

Errors: `IpNotWhitelistedError` `IndeterminateOutcomeError`
`InsufficientBalanceError` `DuplicateReferenceError`
`AccountCredentialRequiredError` `MoneyOutDisabledError`
`WebhookVerificationError` `AuthenticationError` `ConnectionError` `ApiError` —
all extend `SingaPayError`.
